days.title: 1,201 finds
days.pitch: Every geocache I've found as Hipparchus, one dot each, coloured by year. Twenty-odd years of where curiosity has taken me.

days.title: Under my own power
days.pitch: Every run, ride and swim from my Strava archive, drawn as faint lines that stack into a heatmap of the South Sound.
data: Strava bulk export (Settings → My Account → Download your data)

days.title: Every fire around Groveland
days.pitch: Every recorded fire perimeter in Tuolumne County since the early 1900s, oldest faint, newest bright, with the Rim Fire (2013) wrapped around Groveland.
days.alt: Map of Tuolumne County, California, covered in overlapping semi-transparent fire perimeters from 1900 to 2025, pale for old fires and red for recent ones. The 2013 Rim Fire, outlined with a dashed line, fills much of the middle of the county east of Groveland. 36% of the county has burned at least once and 16% twice or more.

days.title: Rainier's swarms
days.pitch: Earthquakes within 30 km of Mount Rainier since 2000, grouped into swarms by space and time. The July 2025 swarm, the largest ever recorded there, stands out.
data: USGS ComCat earthquake catalog (API, no key)
days.alt: Shaded relief map of Mount Rainier with 11,408 earthquakes since 2000 as dots within a 30 km circle. Most are grey background quakes, with coloured clusters marking swarms; the largest, 1,362 quakes in July 2025, sits just under the summit. A bar chart of quakes per month shows a spike for each swarm.

days.title: Where you can see Rainier from
days.pitch: A viewshed from the summit of Mount Rainier over 30 m terrain, with Earth's curvature and refraction, showing every place in Washington with a line of sight to the mountain.
days.alt: Shaded relief map of Washington and northern Oregon with the areas that can see Mount Rainier's summit shaded red: 35,267 square kilometres of land, reaching 390 km to the northwest at the farthest. Cities with a line of sight: Seattle, Tacoma, Lakewood, Olympia, Everett, Victoria, Portland, Yakima, Ellensburg, Aberdeen. Cities without: Bellingham, Vancouver, Salem, Wenatchee, Tri-Cities, Port Angeles, Spokane.

days.title: Tasman to Cook
days.pitch: New Zealand's coast as Abel Tasman charted it in 1642 and James Cook in 1769–70, over the modern coastline, engraved in an 18th-century style. A map version of my Cartographic Perspectives article.
data: David Rumsey Map Collection (Tasman and Cook charts, georeferenced)

days.title: Ten minutes, on the clock
days.pitch: Whatever the day brings, made in ten minutes with a timer visible in the corner of the screenshot.

days.title: Paradise, Eden, Utopia
days.pitch: Every place in the United States named Paradise, Eden, Utopia, Arcadia or Shangri-La, from Paradise on Rainier to Utopia, Texas.
days.alt: Map of the lower 48 states dotted with 836 places named Paradise, Eden, Arcadia, Utopia or Shangri-La. Paradise (501) is the most common, then Eden (243). Only 264 are towns; the most common kinds are townships and other civil divisions, streams, valleys.

days.title: Tacoma to Paradise
days.pitch: One line from the Port of Tacoma to Paradise on Rainier, and what changes along it: people, buildings, trees and elevation.
days.alt: A map of the straight line from the Port of Tacoma to Paradise on Mount Rainier over shaded relief and census population, with two profiles below: people per square kilometre, high in Tacoma and Puyallup and falling to almost none after about km 29, and elevation rising to 8,850 ft on Rainier's flank before Paradise.

days.title: A map made only by asking
days.pitch: A map of Big Creek's watershed near Groveland where every line of code came from prompts, with the prompts posted alongside.

days.title: Where the lahar sirens reach
days.pitch: Pierce County's lahar warning sirens and how far each can be heard, over the lahar zones they protect. Fallback, if the siren locations can't be found: Puget Sound by depth.
data: NOAA Puget Sound coastal elevation model (fallback)

days.title: The Tuolumne powers San Francisco
days.pitch: Hetch Hetchy's dams, the powerhouse at Moccasin just below Groveland, and the lines that carry the Tuolumne's power to San Francisco.
data: EIA U.S. Energy Atlas (power plants, transmission lines)
SFPUC Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System
days.alt: Shaded-relief map from San Francisco east to Yosemite. Gold lines are San Francisco's power lines running from powerhouses below Groveland to the Bay Area; blue is the Hetch Hetchy aqueduct; grey is every other high-voltage line in the region.

days.title: Follow a raindrop
days.pitch: Click anywhere in the Sierra and watch where the water goes, river by river, to the sea, using the USGS's navigation service.
Borges's map the size of the empire, made literal. Big Creek's watershed at full scale as a page you can scroll for miles, with a counter showing how far you've gone.
data: USGS NLDI basin for Big Creek (11284400)

days.title: Inside Kīlauea
days.pitch: The earthquakes beneath Kīlauea's summit in cross-section, sketching the magma plumbing that the surface hides.
days.alt: Left, a shaded-relief map of Kīlauea's summit dotted with 19,466 earthquake epicentres since 2019; right, a north-south cross-section through Halema‘uma‘u showing where the earthquakes cluster with depth.

days.title: Where we've been
days.pitch: A map made with someone else. One option is a trip map built together; another is a public form asking people for their favourite Sierra trailhead, mapped as the answers come in.

days.title: Great Basin's dark sky
days.pitch: Night lights across Nevada and Utah, with Great Basin National Park's dark sky set against the glow of Las Vegas and Salt Lake City.

days.title: Nobody lives here
days.pitch: Nevada's 2020 census blocks with a population of zero. Most of the state is null.
days.alt: Map of Nevada's census blocks: 77% of the land is pale, where nobody lived in 2020; light grey blocks hold a few people each; black specks around Las Vegas, Reno and the towns hold nine in ten Nevadans on 0.4% of the land.

days.title: What the Yakima Valley smells like
days.pitch: Washington's hop acreage by variety, coloured by aroma (citrus, pine, tropical, earthy) from HopLore.
data: USDA NASS National Hop Report (acreage by variety and state)

days.title: Kangaroo rats in hexagons
days.pitch: Every Dipodomys observation across the Southwest and Great Basin, binned into H3 hexagons. A return to my 2023 Day 1.
days.alt: Hexagon map of western North America shaded by how many kangaroo rat records each holds, 94,547 in all across 1,625 hexagons; the busiest holds 3,054. Death Valley is marked.

days.title: Groveland, by volunteers
days.pitch: Everything OpenStreetMap knows about Groveland and Big Oak Flat, after I add what's missing.

days.title: The world from Lakewood
days.pitch: An azimuthal equidistant map centred on Lakewood, where straight lines from the centre are true distances, to everywhere I've been, from Namibia to Guadeloupe.
days.alt: A round world map centred on Lakewood, Washington, in an azimuthal equidistant projection, with red lines out to Groveland (1,054 km), Reno (877 km), Ruby Mountains (923 km), Namibia (15,332 km), Guadeloupe (6,491 km).

days.title: Every brewery I've checked into
days.pitch: My Untappd check-ins, mapped by brewery, sized by how many beers.

days.title: Every stream that reaches Modesto
days.pitch: The whole Tuolumne river network above Modesto, by stream order, with the SIERRA-FLOW gages on it.
days.alt: Map of the Tuolumne River basin above Modesto, 4,742 square kilometres of the Sierra Nevada, with 3,825 kilometres of streams drawn thicker by stream order up to order 6, and the five SIERRA-FLOW gages marked.

days.title: A day of ground motion
days.pitch: A 24-hour helicorder from Camp Muir on Rainier, one line per hour. A map of time, or of a place?
days.alt: A helicorder: 24 horizontal wiggly lines, one per hour of July 8, 2025, recorded at Camp Muir on Mount Rainier, in alternating ink, red, blue and green. Gold dots mark the 352 earthquakes located nearby that day.

days.title: Lake Tahoe, clear and deep
days.pitch: Tahoe's depth and its clarity: how far down a Secchi disk can be seen, from the SECCHI dashboard's data.
days.alt: Map of Lake Tahoe's floor shaded blue by depth to 497 m, with 100 m contours and the deepest point marked.

days.title: Something I've never used
days.pitch: Every building in Washington from Overture Maps, queried with DuckDB's spatial extension and drawn with lonboard. Both new to me.

days.title: Did you feel it? Nisqually, 2001
days.pitch: The M6.8 Nisqually earthquake of February 28, 2001, as the people who felt it reported it, from USGS "Did You Feel It?".
data: USGS ComCat event uw10530748, DYFI product
days.alt: Map of the Pacific Northwest showing how strongly people felt the magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake of February 28, 2001. Small squares coloured from pale (weak) to dark red (very strong) cover western Washington, strongest around the epicenter at the south end of Puget Sound near Olympia, Lakewood and Tacoma, and fading toward Portland, Vancouver and Spokane. Based on 10,725 'Did You Feel It?' reports.

days.title: Rainier's snow from space
days.pitch: A season of snow cover on Rainier from satellite, draped over the mountain.
data: MODIS / Sentinel-2 snow cover (via the Rainier Snowpack Tracker)

days.title: Groveland from memory
days.pitch: Groveland drawn by hand from memory, then laid over the real map to see what I remembered and what I didn't.
